div.b: API keys are locked to the region they were created in

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 648px; height: 1px; padding-top: 637px; margin-left: 19px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
A key made for one region will not authenticate against another
region’s endpoint, and the rejection looks exactly like a wrong key.
This costs more debugging time than any other single thing in
this pillar.
Decide the region first, on data residency grounds, then create
keys in it. Correcting it later means reissuing every key.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 664px; height: 1px; padding-top: 617px; margin-left: 717px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #00294D;

display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 648px; height: 1px; padding-top: 637px; margin-left: 719px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
The scan endpoint authenticates with an API key in an x-pan-token
header. The management endpoint authenticates with an OAuth
bearer token from a service account.
They are not interchangeable, and presenting one to the other is a
common early confusion. You only need the second if keys and
profiles will be created programmatically.
